title: Deployment Curation Cadence & Comm Lane (v2) — draft
content:
Purpose:
This note defines a lightweight, repeatable cadence for 'deployment curation' — the act of selecting, shaping, and communicating a set of customers/traffic slices for each release window — and the associated communications lane (comm-lane) behaviors for on-call and stakeholder signals. Intention is to reduce blast radius while keeping release velocity.

Context / motivation:
- We frequently ship changes that are safe for 90% of traffic but have edge cases at the tails (very long sequences, unusual token distributions, private quantized models).
- Traditional canaries are binary (on/off) and miss nuanced segment composition. Curation cadence formalizes gradual surface area expansion tied to measurable signals.
- This doc is an operational sketch for release engineers and product owners to run an explicit, observable rollout with clear comm expectations.

High-level cadence (weekly sprint-aligned):
1) Tuesday - Curation Plan (EOD): product + release lead publish the curated slices for the upcoming deploy window. Keep the list <= 6 slices.
2) Wednesday - Dry-run and synthetic smoke: run curated slices through the staging traffic simulator and the metrics probes.
3) Thursday - Preflight uplift (limited real traffic): enable change for slice-1 (~1% global traffic or dedicated customers). Monitor 2 hours.
4) Thursday night - Expand to slice-2 if all green (3% traffic). 12-hour watch.
5) Friday - Regional expansion (APAC/EU) for slices 1–2. Saturday morning: if green, broaden to slice-3.
6) Sunday - Full sweep if 72h of stable signals.

Curated slice selection guidance (keep it pragmatic):
- Slice definition examples: "enterprise-paying customers with retention >90d and eval set X", "customers using long-sequence API (seq>8k)", "private deployment tenants on v1.2 stack".
- Prioritize: low-number-of-customers with high-impact signals (so we can pivot quickly), then high-volume low-risk slices.
- Never mix cross-region expansion with a model-architecture change in the same window unless explicitly approved.

Preflight checklist (to be ticked before enabling slice-1):
- [ ] Release branch built and smoke-tested: build id and artifact SHA noted.
- [ ] Migration plan for KV cache / schema changes: rollback steps documented.
- [ ] Canary config uploaded to control-plane and verified in canary UI.
- [ ] Telemetry queries (perf + correctness) created and saved as dashboard filters (list query ids).
- [ ] Alert thresholds defined and assigned to shift owners: latency > p95 baseline + 30%, error_rate > 0.5% absolute, hallucination metric regression > 2% — (see signal definitions lower).
- [ ] Stakeholder comm-lane message drafted and scheduled (Slack #deployments and product email brief).
- [ ] Pager duty rotation assigned: primary, secondary, and escalation contacts for the 72h window.

Comm-lane behavior (what to post, when):
- Pre-deploy (T-24h): post plan summary to #deployments and ping product leads. Include curated slices, expected users impacted, and mitigation links.
- On-deploy (T0): update thread with artifact SHA, enabled-slices list, and first-watch window duration.
- On-signal: follow template - TL;DR, signal, severity (S1–S3), mitigation step, next check-in time. Keep updates every 30m until S2 resolved, 15m for S1.
- Post-resolution: short postmortem stub in-thread within 4 hours. Full writeup if S1 within 48 hours.

Key signals & example queries (ops-friendly descriptions):
- Perf regressions: p50/p95 latency by route and model variant. Query: latency_by_route_7d_anchor (dashboard id: perf-anchors-12).
- Error surface: rate of non-200s responses and internal exception tags. Query: backend-errors-by-tag-14.
- Quality regressions: prompt-set eval pass-rate change over baseline; for token-level regression, run delta-bleu and hallucination heuristics. Query: eval-suite-delta-3.
- Customer-facing anomalies: spike in support tickets tied to release artifact id (search support-tags: artifact-<sha>).

Micro-rollback drill (fast-path rollback template):
1) If S1 triggered: immediate traffic switch to last-known-good model variant via control-plane toggle (document toggle id).
2) Scale down new instances and drain connections.
3) Roll forward mitigation: if rollback causes downstream issues, open emergency bridge and route traffic to dedicated read-only pool.
4) Assign owner to run 'forensics-lite' — collect logs, trace ids, KV cache digests.

Release notes draft (to be included in customer-facing changelog if rollout completes without S1 in 72h):
- Title: "Model serving improvements and safety fixes — v2027.03.curation"
- Short summary: "Performance optimizations for long-sequence workloads and improved fallback routing for quantized models. Smaller correctness fixes for stable generation observed in internal evals."
- Impacted surfaces: API text-generate, chat-streaming, private deployments (v1.2 opt-in).
- Migrations: None required for most customers. If you run custom KV-cache workloads, see migration steps in CONFLUENCE-REQ-2345.
- Rollout: phased via curated slices; full availability expected after extended watch (3 days).

Operational notes / heuristics (notes to self):
- Keep slice lists explicit and compact. If slice grows >6, break into two windows.
- Weekend windows: prefer read-only or low-risk changes only (defaults to no architecture changes Saturday–Sunday).
- If a regression only shows on long-sequence prompts, avoid slicing by customer type; instead slice by route + request_length to minimize collateral.

Calendar sketch (example week):
- Mon 09:00 — Release sync (30m) — finalize curated slices
- Tue 17:00 — Publish curation list + comm draft
- Wed 03:00 — Synthetic dry-run (region-sim)
- Thu 11:00 — Enable slice-1 (1% traffic)
- Thu 20:00 — Expand to slice-2 (3%) if green
- Fri 07:00 — Regional APAC enable for slice-1/2
- Sun 09:00 — Decision point: proceed to full or hold (meeting note)

Outstanding questions (to resolve before next iteration):
- Who owns final sign-off: product lead or release engineering? (proposal: release eng signs for infra, product signs for UX/quality)
- How do we codify slice membership in the control plane to allow automatic reversal? (feature ticket needed)
- Should we record a small voice check-in (1m) in addition to text updates for S1s? Quick wins vs noise.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Priya: prototype a slice-definition schema in control-plane (ticket JIRA-RELEASE-1129) — due 2027-03-10.
- Ethan: create standard dashboard queries and save-as templates (perf + quality) — due 2027-03-05.
- Marina: draft customer-facing blurb for the notes and sample rollback FAQ — due 2027-03-08.
- Samir: run a rehearsal on 2027-03-12 with simulated slice expansion and timeboxed failures.

Appendix — quick templates:
- Comm-lane headline template: [DEPLOY][<team>] <artifact-sha> enabled for <slice-id> — watch window <hours> — owners: <primary>/<secondary>.
- On-signal update template: [SIG][S<level>] <short desc> | impact <users/%> | mitigation <step> | next <ETA>.

Rough log (scratch):
- 2027-02-20: initial sketch — Priya.
- 2027-02-22: added comm-lane templates and threshold suggestions — Ethan.
- 2027-02-26: adjusted week cadence to avoid regional expansion at T0 — Marina.

This is intentionally light-weight and iterative. The aim is to make curated rollouts easy to describe, instrument, and reverse. Feedback welcome — leave comments in the doc or ping me in #release-cadence.
